newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Eskom not to sell 2 power stations.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Eskom not to sell 2 power stations.

text.p: State-run electricity generator Eskom will not proceed with the sale of the decommissioned Taaibos and Highveld power stations, despite the placing of advertisements for tenders this week, the government said on Thursday.

"Eskom has conceded that the decision to advertise for tenders was an error of judgement on their part and that the advertisements will be withdrawn immediately," the Ministry of Public Enterprises said in a statement.
The future of the decommissioned power stations would be discussed within the Restructuring and Transformation Committee, as agreed between the government, labour and management, the ministry said.

An advertisement in this week's Financial Mail said the two stations -- each consisting of eight 60 MW steam turbine generators, boilers and precipitators -- were being offered for sale on a closed tender basis.
The company had set a closing date of March 14 for tenders, which excluded the possibility of generating electricity on site.
Eskom has recently moved into the limelight as South Africa's privatisation drive slowly gains momentum but plans to sell mothballed stations have been opposed by labour unions.
Concerns centre around job losses and the potential loss of state control in a vital sector of the economy.
Government, unions and Eskom have been trying to settle fundamental differences on the approach to restructuring the electricity giant in the Restructuring and Transformation Committee.

Labour at the beginning of the year walked out of the committee, raising concerns about the possible sale of mothballed power stations or recommissioning of decommissioned plants; a planned outsourcing deal between Eskom and IBM South Africa Group Ltd ; an internal regrouping of management within Eskom; and the structuring of the electricity distribution sector.

But representatives of the National Union of Mineworkers and the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa subsequently agreed to come back on board to continue restructuring talks with government and Eskom.
